hero.filename: Irish Peace Park, Messines 1917 Battle plaque.jpg
hero.caption: An elevated bronze plaque showing the direction of assault at the outset of the Battle of Messines in June 1917 in which the two voluntary Irish divisions, the 36th (Ulster) Division and the 16th (Irish) Division, played a decisive role. The plaque stands in the grounds of the Island of Ireland Peace Park, Messines, Belgium.
hero.alt: An elevated bronze plaque showing the direction of assault at the outset of the Battle of Messines in June 1917 in which the two voluntary Irish divisions, the 36th (Ulster) Division and the 16th (Irish) Division, played a decisive role. The plaque stands in the grounds of the Island of Ireland Peace Park, Messines, Belgium.

images.filename: NLS Haig - Smashed up German trench on Messines Ridge with dead.jpg
images.caption: This is a disturbing image of a destroyed German trench. In the foreground the limp bodies of dead German soldiers lie amidst the rubble. It is difficult to distinguish the soldiers from the chaos around them, but four bodies are clearly visible. One man, wearing a helmet, has been pushed forward by the blast and, although dead, appears to crouch forward. The entire scene is a maelstrom of mud, splintered wood and dead bodies.Original reads: 'OFFICIAL PHOTOGRAPHS TAKEN ON THE BRITISH WESTERN FRONT. Smashed up German trench on Messines Ridge with dead.'Photographs from the Haig "Official Photographs" series
